questions.question: Which Russian scientist is credited with developing the periodic table?
options: John Dalton
Dimitri Mendeleev
Ernest Rutherford
Marie Curie

questions.question: In the periodic table, what are the columns and the rows called?
options: Columns are called groups, and rows are called periods.
Columns are called periods, and rows are called groups.
Columns are called families, and rows are called categories.
Columns are called elements, and rows are called compounds.

questions.question: Which group of the periodic table contains the noble gases, which are known for being unreactive?
options: Group 1
Group 2
Group 0
Group 7

questions.question: What is the physical state of all noble gases when kept at room temperature?
options: Liquid
Gas
Solid
Aqueous

questions.question: Why are the noble gases in Group 0 chemically stable and unreactive?
options: They have complete outer electron shells.
They have very low atomic masses.
They exist only as single atoms in a liquid state.
They have more protons than electrons.

questions.question: As you move down Group 0 of the periodic table, what happens to the atomic mass, density, and boiling points of the elements?
options: Atomic mass increases, but density and boiling points decrease.
Atomic mass and density increase, but boiling points decrease.
Atomic mass, density, and boiling points all decrease.
Atomic mass, density, and boiling points all increase.

questions.question: How do the properties of elements within any specific group typically change as you move down the group?
options: They change suddenly and unpredictably.
They remain exactly identical for all elements.
They change gradually down the group.
They only change for the first two elements and then stop.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the trends and properties of Group 1 metals as you go down the group?
options: They are hard, dense, and become less reactive.
They are soft, have lower densities than most other metals, and become more reactive.
They are soft, have high densities, and become less reactive.
They are hard, have lower densities than most other metals, and become less reactive.

questions.question: Why are Group 1 metals called alkali metals?
options: They react with dilute acids to form acidic salts.
They react with water to form an alkaline solution and hydrogen gas.
They dissolve in water to produce pure liquid alkali.
They burn in air to form an alkaline gas.

questions.question: What products are formed when Group 2 metals react with dilute acids?
options: A metal oxide and water
A metal hydroxide and hydrogen gas
A salt and hydrogen gas
A salt and water

questions.question: How does the reactivity of Group 2 metals compare to Group 1 metals in the same period?
options: Group 2 metals are more reactive.
Group 2 metals are less reactive.
They have the exact same level of reactivity.
Group 2 metals do not react at all, whereas Group 1 metals are highly reactive.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes the elements in Group 7 of the periodic table?
options: They are shiny metals that form alkaline solutions.
They are all non-metals that have coloured vapours, most of which are toxic.
They are unreactive, colourless gases that do not form compounds.
They are highly dense metals that are liquid at room temperature.

questions.question: How does the state of the elements in Group 7 at room temperature change as you move down the group?
options: From solid to liquid to gas
From liquid to gas
From gas to solid
From solid to gas

questions.question: What is the trend in chemical reactivity as you go down Group 7?
options: Reactivity increases.
Reactivity decreases.
Reactivity remains completely unchanged.
Reactivity decreases then suddenly increases at the bottom.

questions.question: What is formed when halogens react with Group 1 and Group 2 metals?
options: Metal hydroxides
Metal oxides
Metal halides
Metal carbonates

questions.question: Which of the following is a key physical property of metal halides?
options: They are completely insoluble in water.
They are soluble in water.
They are highly volatile gases at room temperature.
They cannot dissolve in liquid water.

questions.question: What can we expect about the properties of elements that reside in the same group of the periodic table?
options: They have completely different chemical behaviours.
They have similar properties.
They have identical boiling points and masses.
Their properties have no relationship to one another.

questions.question: In addition to groups and periods, into what two main categories can elements in the periodic table be divided?
options: Reactive and unreactive gases
Solids and liquids only
Non-metals and metals, which include the transition metals
Synthetic elements and natural gases
